title: Topological triviality of mu-constant families of surface singularities
main_claim: Every holomorphic one-parameter mu-constant family of isolated hypersurface singularities in C^3 is topologically right-trivial (surface case of the Lê–Ramanujam/mu-constant problem). Route: (i) mult 2 / log canonical cases via Teissier's mu* criterion and Whitney-based lifting; (ii) non-lc case: prove constancy of Wahl's invariant beta=-P·P by a semistable dlt log model over an algebraic curve, a nearby-Euler comparison 0=sum chi_c(S_a°)+delta with delta>=0 (Greuel–Steenbrink), and Langer's log BMY 0<=(K+B)^2<=3chi_c(S_a°); then Okuma's CMH 2004 Thm 1.2 gives a simultaneous minimal semigood resolution with reduced exceptional restrictions, Euler constancy rules out node smoothing (relative normal crossings), complete lifts on the punctured zero family extend to ambient levels, and the finite base change is removed by a seam correction.
coverage: Read all main sections (2–14) line by line and the start of appendix 15 (supported-square lemma, statement of the marked monomial reduction); appendix 16 is an alternative criterion and was not used in the main chain. Checked by hand: the Lemma 3.2 identity beta=K_V^2-(K_S+B)^2 (P=rho^*K_V+Z_P, the cross term vanishes); the compactification numbers K^2=d(d-4)^2 and chi=d(d^2-4d+6)-mu-1; the finite-determinacy and jet-locus arguments; the negativity-lemma support argument; the boundary-cover and nearby-Euler vanishing (inclusion–exclusion for (1-1)^h and products of torus fibers); the sign cancellation, which forces every extra (K_{S_a}+B)^2 to be 0; the square specialization; the node-count Euler argument; continuity at the axis in the ambient tube lemma; the seam identity H_{ζr}∘J_r=H_r; and the mult-3 lc case, mu*=(2,4,mu). I fetched Okuma's CMH 2004 paper and confirmed that Thm 1.2 gives exactly what is used: after base change, fibrewise minimal semigood resolutions with E_t reduced and supported on f^{-1}(γ(t)), for small deformations of a non-lc Gorenstein germ with -P_t·P_t constant. These cited results were taken on trust in their stated forms: Langer's Cor. 5.2 and Thm 7.6 (log BMY, and zero local orbifold weight on lc boundary points), the KM 7.9 semistable MMP, the marked toroidal semistable reduction, Greuel–Steenbrink, Varchenko's spectrum constancy, the Fernández de Bobadilla–Pełka equimultiplicity theorem, and Teissier's criterion.
sibling_notes: The family-064 board was empty when I started. Useful for siblings: Okuma CMH 79 (2004) Thm 1.2 really does give (1) minimal semigood fibre resolutions and (2) reduced E_t equal to the full reduced inverse image of the section. It does not give a weak simultaneous resolution (constant graph) except in the star-shaped case. This paper does not need one, because it proves relative normal crossings separately with an Euler-characteristic argument.
